15: ANÍSYA. What? MÍTRITCH. Nikíta isn't back from town, is he?
13: MÍTRITCH [ an old labourer, enters, and slowly takes off his outdoor things ] Oh Lord, have mercy! Well, hasn't the master come home yet?
12: Curtain. The same hut. Winter. Nine months have passed since Act II . Anísya, plainly dressed, sits before a loom weaving. Nan is on the oven.
11: A VOICE IN THE CROWD. Send for the old women to lay out the body. MATRYÓNA [ rolls up her sleeves ] Is there any water in the copper? But I daresay the samovár is still hot. I'll also go and help a bit.
9: Enter Neighbour. Matryóna and Neighbour catch hold of Anísya under the arms to support her. Akoulína and Martha go into the hut. A crowd assembles.
7: ANÍSYA [ runs out screaming. Clings to a post, and begins wailing ] [4] Oh, oh, ah! who-o-o-m have you left me to, why-y-y have you dese-e-e-e-rted me—a miserable widow … to live my life alone … Why have you closed your bright eyes …
5: MATRYÓNA. I'm from Zoúevo. I'm Nikíta's mother from Zoúevo, my dearie. Good afternoon to you. He's withering, withering away, poor dear—your brother, I mean. He came out himself. “Send for my sister,” he said, “because,” said he … Dear me, why, I do believe, he's dead!
3: MARTHA [ pointing to Matryóna ] Who's that?
1: AKOULÍNA [ puts down the clothes ] Don't know, I've been to the river.
